Assume Countable Choice for the smooth Lorentzian tangent-bundle conventions of the suppliers. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, $r_0>0$, and $\mathcal E=I\times(r_0,\infty)\times S^2$, where $S^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ has its unit round metric $q_{AB}$ and area form $d\Omega$. Let $D_A$ be the Levi-Civita covariant derivative of $q$, and raise angular indices with $q^{AB}$. A **Bondi-Sachs end** is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $\mathcal E$ written in coordinates $(u,r,x^A)$, $A,B=1,2$, as

$$g=-\left(e^{2\beta}\frac Vr-r^2\gamma_{AB}U^AU^B\right)du^2-2e^{2\beta}du\,dr-2r^2\gamma_{AB}U^Bdu\,dx^A+r^2\gamma_{AB}dx^A dx^B,$$

where $\beta,V,U^A,\gamma_{AB}$ are smooth, $\gamma_{AB}$ is positive definite, $\gamma^{AC}\gamma_{CB}=\delta^A_B$, and $\det(\gamma_{AB})=\det(q_{AB})$. Thus $u=\mathrm{constant}$ are outgoing null hypersurfaces, $r$ is the area radius, and $x^A$ are constant along their null generators. This Bondi gauge has $g_{rr}=g_{rA}=0$.

A **smooth Bondi expansion** is such an end with the differentiated uniform expansions

$$\gamma_{AB}=q_{AB}+\frac{C_{AB}(u,x)}r+\frac{P_{AB}(u,x)}{r^2}+O(r^{-3}),\qquad \beta=O(r^{-2}),\qquad U^A=\frac{U^A_{(2)}(u,x)}{r^2}+\frac{U^A_{(3)}(u,x)}{r^3}+O(r^{-4}),\qquad V=r-2m(u,x)+\frac{V_{(1)}(u,x)}r+O(r^{-2}).$$

Here $C_{AB}$, $P_{AB}$ and the displayed coefficients are smooth sphere fields on $I$; the determinant gauge imposes $q^{AB}C_{AB}=0$ and $q^{AB}P_{AB}=\tfrac12 C_{AB}C^{AB}$. For every compact $I'\subset I$, angular chart compact set, and derivative multi-index $\alpha$ of total order at most two, the partial derivatives of each $O(r^{-k})$ remainder obey $\partial_u^{\alpha_u}D^{\alpha_x}\partial_r^{\alpha_r}O(r^{-k})=O(r^{-k-\alpha_r})$ uniformly as $r\to\infty$. Define the **mass aspect** by $m(u,x):=-\tfrac12\lim_{r\to\infty}(V(u,r,x)-r)$, the **Bondi shear** by $C_{AB}=\lim_{r\to\infty}r(\gamma_{AB}-q_{AB})$, the **Bondi news** by $N_{AB}:=\partial_u C_{AB}$, and the **geometric Bondi mass** by $m_B(u):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}m(u,x)\,d\Omega$. The future null boundary used here is the formal $r\to\infty$ boundary $\mathcal I^+=I\times S^2$ with coordinates $(u,x^A)$; no conformal completion is included in this definition.

A **vacuum Bondi expansion** is a smooth Bondi expansion whose Ricci tensor vanishes identically on the supplied end: $\operatorname{Ric}_g(p)=0$ for every $p\in\mathcal E$. Equivalently, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(u,r,x)=0$ for every pair $a,b\in\{u,r,1,2\}$ at every point of every Bondi coordinate chart, with no cosmological term. The curvature convention is $R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$, $R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=R^a{}_{bcd}\partial_a$, and $\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=R^a{}_{bad}$. This is a condition on the supplied metric, not an assertion of existence for prescribed boundary coefficients. Imposing only finitely many asymptotic coefficient equations does not assert membership in this vacuum subclass; formal boundary-data examples must state separately which equations they impose.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. Tensoriality of $R$ is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a).
Lowering its output slot with the smooth metric and contracting with the
smooth inverse metric are intrinsic tensor operations
([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] clauses (b)-(c),
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]]). Thus these formulas give smooth
fields of types $(0,4)$, $(0,2)$, $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$, respectively,
independent of the chart. Symmetry of $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $G$ is proved
separately in [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clause (d).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let $R$ be
the curvature operator of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
with components $R^a{}_{bcd}$ in a chart.

**(a) Tensoriality.** For all smooth functions $f$ on $M$ and smooth vector
fields $X,Y,Z$ on a common domain, $R(X,Y)Z=-R(Y,X)Z$ and
$$R(fX,Y)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,fY)Z=fR(X,Y)Z,\qquad R(X,Y)(fZ)=fR(X,Y)Z .$$
Consequently, for every $p\in M$, the value $R(X,Y)Z|_p$ depends only on
$X_p,Y_p,Z_p$, and $R$ is a smooth tensor field of type $(1,3)$ on $M$ whose
components in every smooth chart are the functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ of
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] clause (b).

**(b) Coordinate formula.** In every smooth chart $(U,x)$ with Christoffel
symbols $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of $\nabla$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]),
$$R^a{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^a{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^a{}_{cb} +\sum_e\bigl(\Gamma^a{}_{ce}\Gamma^e{}_{db}-\Gamma^a{}_{de}\Gamma^e{}_{cb}\bigr)$$
on $U$, for all $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.

**(c) Point-normal formula.** If the chart is point-normal at $p$, that is
$g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$ and $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$
([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]), then, writing
$g_{ad,bc}:=\partial_b\partial_cg_{ad}$,
$$R_{abcd}(p)=\tfrac12\bigl(g_{ad,bc}+g_{bc,ad}-g_{bd,ac}-g_{ac,bd}\bigr)(p) .$$
Equivalently, $R^a{}_{bcd}(p)=\tfrac12\,g^{ae}(p)\bigl(\partial_b\partial_cg_{ed}
+\partial_e\partial_dg_{bc}-\partial_e\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dg_{ec}\bigr)(p)$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Metric compatibility and zero torsion give $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12g^{ad}(\partial_bg_{cd}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc})$: lower the output index in metric compatibility and add the two cyclic equations minus the third. Multiplication of the Bondi metric by $g^{ur}=-E^{-1}$, $g^{rr}=E^{-1}V/r$, $g^{rA}=-E^{-1}U^A$, $g^{AB}=h^{AB}$ and $g^{uu}=g^{uA}=0$ gives the identity matrix. Its determinant is $-E^2r^4\det q$. Differentiating a determinant gives $\Gamma^a{}_{ab}=\partial_b\log\sqrt{|\det g|}$, so the traces are exactly $T_u:=\Gamma^a{}_{au}=2\dot\beta$, $T_r:=\Gamma^a{}_{ar}=2/r+2\beta_r$ and $T_A:=\Gamma^a{}_{aA}=Q_A+2\beta_A$. In particular $\operatorname{tr}(\gamma^{-1}\dot\gamma)=0$ exactly; no trace-free part of $P_{AB}$ has been removed. Contracting [F3] using [F2] gives $\operatorname{Ric}_{bc}=\partial_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\partial_cT_b+\Gamma^a{}_{bc}T_a-\Gamma^a{}_{cd}\Gamma^d{}_{ba}$.

The given differentiated expansions imply $E=1+O(r^{-2})$, $h_{AB}=r^2q_{AB}+rC_{AB}+O(1)$, $h^{AB}=r^{-2}q^{AB}-r^{-3}C^{AB}+O(r^{-4})$, $g_{uu}=-1+2m/r+O(r^{-2})$ and $g_{uA}=-w_A+O(r^{-1})$. These follow directly from $g_{uu}=-EV/r+h_{AB}U^AU^B$ and $g_{uA}=-h_{AB}U^B$. A radial derivative lowers each remainder's order by one, and time or angular derivatives through total order two preserve its order. Products and inverses have these same differentiated bounds, since their denominators tend uniformly to nonzero ones. Every differentiated expression below uses at most two derivatives of the metric coefficients. Thus these are the existing differentiated hypotheses, not a termwise differentiability assumption beyond them.

For the radial constraint put $H^B{}_A:=\Gamma^B{}_{rA}$ and $T^r{}_A:=\Gamma^r{}_{rA}$. The Christoffel formula of step 1.1 gives the exact identities $\Gamma^u{}_{rA}=0$, $\Gamma^u{}_{rr}=\Gamma^B{}_{rr}=0$, $\Gamma^r{}_{rr}=2\beta_r$, $H^B{}_A=\tfrac12h^{BC}\partial_rh_{AC}$, and $T^r{}_A=\beta_A+(2E)^{-1}h_{AB}\partial_rU^B$. Hence $H^B{}_A=\delta^B_A/r-C^B{}_A/(2r^2)+O(r^{-3})$ and $T^r{}_A=-w_A/r+O(r^{-2})$. Also $\Gamma^u{}_{AB}=(2E)^{-1}\partial_rh_{AB}=O(r)$ and $\Gamma^B{}_{ru}=\tfrac12h^{BC}(\partial_rg_{uC}+\partial_CE)=O(r^{-4})$. The angular symbols are exactly $\Gamma^C{}_{AB}=\Gamma[\gamma]^C{}_{AB}+(2E)^{-1}U^C\partial_rh_{AB}$. Their difference from the round connection is $S^C{}_{AB}:=\Gamma^C{}_{AB}-\Gamma[q]^C{}_{AB}=\{D_AC^C{}_B+D_BC^C{}_A-D^CC_{AB}\}/(2r)+w^Cq_{AB}/r+O(r^{-2})$, obtained by inserting $\gamma=q+C/r+O(r^{-2})$ in its connection formula. Since $q^{AB}C_{AB}=0$, its contracted leading coefficient is $S^C{}_{AC}=w_A/r+O(r^{-2})$.

For the supplementary coefficient, set $K^a{}_b:=\Gamma^a{}_{ub}$. Using the exact traces from step 1.1 and combining $\partial_AK^A{}_u+Q_AK^A{}_u=D_AK^A{}_u$, the Ricci formula is exactly $\operatorname{Ric}_{uu}=\partial_uK^u{}_u+\partial_rK^r{}_u+D_AK^A{}_u-2\ddot\beta+2\dot\beta K^u{}_u+(2/r+2\beta_r)K^r{}_u+2\beta_AK^A{}_u-K^a{}_bK^b{}_a$. The Christoffel formula gives $K^u{}_u=2\dot\beta+(2E)^{-1}\partial_rg_{uu}$ exactly. It also gives $K^r{}_u=-\dot m/r+O(r^{-2})$ and $K^A{}_u=-\dot w^A/r^2+O(r^{-3})$: the leading terms come respectively from $\tfrac12g^{ru}\partial_ug_{uu}$ and $h^{AB}\partial_ug_{uB}$, while all other terms have the indicated lower orders. Therefore $\partial_uK^u{}_u-2\ddot\beta=-\dot m/r^2+O(r^{-3})$, $\partial_rK^r{}_u=\dot m/r^2+O(r^{-3})$, $D_AK^A{}_u=-D_A\dot w^A/r^2+O(r^{-3})$ and $(2/r)K^r{}_u=-2\dot m/r^2+O(r^{-3})$. The remaining three terms involving a derivative of $\beta$ times a $K$ are $O(r^{-4})$. The remainder differentiations here are covered by step 2.1.

Expand the contracted Ricci formula of step 1.1 for $(b,c)=(r,A)$. The angular derivative and background-connection terms combine into $D_BH^B{}_A$. The derivative $-\partial_AT_r=-2\partial_A\beta_r$ is $O(r^{-3})$. In the final quadratic sum, the only non-background terms possibly of order $r^{-2}$ are $S^C{}_{AB}H^B{}_C$ and $H^C{}_AT^r{}_C$: their coefficients are respectively $w_A$ and $-w_A$, by step 3.1, so they cancel. The other potentially large product $\Gamma^u{}_{AB}\Gamma^B{}_{ru}$ is $O(r^{-3})$; products with $\Gamma^u{}_{rA},\Gamma^u{}_{rr},\Gamma^B{}_{rr}$ vanish, and products involving $\beta_r$ or $\beta_A$ are $O(r^{-3})$ or smaller. Consequently $\operatorname{Ric}_{rA}=\partial_rT^r{}_A+D_BH^B{}_A+(2/r)T^r{}_A+O(r^{-3})=r^{-2}(-w_A-\tfrac12D_BC^B{}_A)+O(r^{-3})$. The first, second and third terms contribute respectively $w_A$, $-\tfrac12D_BC^B{}_A$ and $-2w_A$. Vacuum [A2] therefore gives $w^A=-\tfrac12D_BC^{AB}$ without determining $U^A_{(3)}$ or any trace-free coefficient of $P_{AB}$.

To exhibit every possible quadratic contribution, the same Christoffel formula gives $K^u{}_r=0$, $K^u{}_A=\beta_A+(2E)^{-1}\partial_rg_{uA}=O(r^{-2})$, $K^r{}_r=O(r^{-2})$, $K^r{}_A=O(r^{-1})$, $K^A{}_r=O(r^{-4})$, and $K^A{}_B=\tfrac12h^{AC}\partial_uh_{BC}+O(r^{-2})=N^A{}_B/(2r)+O(r^{-2})$; also $K^u{}_u=O(r^{-2})$, $K^r{}_u=O(r^{-1})$ and $K^A{}_u=O(r^{-2})$ by step 3.2. Thus in $K^a{}_bK^b{}_a$ the $uu$ and $rr$ diagonal products are $O(r^{-4})$, the $ur$ pair vanishes, the $uA$ pair is $O(r^{-4})$, the $rA$ pair is $O(r^{-5})$, and only the angular block contributes at order $r^{-2}$, giving $K^A{}_BK^B{}_A=N_{AB}N^{AB}/(4r^2)+O(r^{-3})$. This exhausts the contraction, rather than omitting uncomputed subleading terms.

Combining steps 3.2 and 4.2 proves $\operatorname{Ric}_{uu}=r^{-2}(-2\dot m-D_A\dot w^A-\tfrac14N_{AB}N^{AB})+O(r^{-3})$. The determinant identity in step 1.1 cancelled the entire time derivative of the angular determinant before expansion; in particular its $r^{-2}$ trace combination $\operatorname{tr}_qP-\tfrac12C_{AB}C^{AB}$ and its first two time derivatives vanish. All remaining occurrences of $P_{AB}$ in the angular $K$ block have order $r^{-2}$ and hence enter its square only at $r^{-3}$ or below. Similarly $U^A_{(3)}$ affects $K^A{}_u$ only at $r^{-3}$ and $K^r{}_u$ only at $r^{-2}$, while $V_{(1)}$ affects the latter only at $r^{-2}$; radial differentiation or multiplication by $2/r$ then lowers these to $r^{-3}$. No coefficient called $\beta_{(3)}$ need exist: the whole $\beta$ time-derivative cancellation is exact, and the remaining derivative products have already been bounded. Since $q$ and $D$ do not depend on $u$, step 4.1 gives $D_A\dot w^A=-\tfrac12D_AD_BN^{AB}$. Vacuum [A2] now makes the displayed $r^{-2}$ coefficient zero and yields $\partial_um=\tfrac14D_AD_BN^{AB}-\tfrac18N_{AB}N^{AB}$, with no additional choice use or asymptotic restriction.

Let $(M,g,N)=(\mathbb R^4,\eta,\partial_0)$ be the flat model with its
inertial chart $x$ and metric components
$\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$
([[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). Since the chart identifies each
$T_p\mathbb R^4$ with $\mathbb R^4$, all objects below are defined by their
components in this chart; they are the components at a point, and a subscript
$p$ is suppressed. Indices are raised and lowered with $\eta$ and $\eta^{-1}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]), and orthogonality is in
the sense of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]].

**observer** of the flat model: $n$ is future-directed, $\eta(n,n)=-1$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]); and let
$s=s^a\partial_a$ be a **propagation direction**: $\eta(s,s)=1$ and
$\eta(n,s)=0$. The pair defines the two-dimensional **screen**
$\Sigma(n,s):=\{v\in\mathbb R^4:\eta(v,n)=0,\ \eta(v,s)=0\}$, on which the
restriction of $\eta$ is positive definite by
[[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]. The **screen projector** and
the **spatial projector** of the pair are the $(1,1)$-tensors with components

$$p^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b-s^as_b,\qquad h^a{}_b:=\delta^a{}_b+n^an_b,$$

and the covariant form of the screen projector is
$p_{ab}:=\eta_{ac}p^c{}_b=\eta_{ab}+n_an_b-s_as_b$. The properties $p^2=p$,
$h^2=h$, $\operatorname{im}p=\Sigma(n,s)$ and $\operatorname{im}h=n^\perp$
are proved in the screen-projector lemma of this page.

**(b) TT projection.** Let $A=(A_{ab})$ be a symmetric covariant $2$-tensor
at a point. Its **transverse-traceless (TT) projection with respect to
$(n,s)$** is the symmetric covariant $2$-tensor

$$\Pi_{n,s}(A)_{ab}:=p_a{}^cp_b{}^dA_{cd}-\tfrac12\,p_{ab}\,p^{cd}A_{cd},\qquad p^{cd}:=\eta^{ce}\eta^{df}p_{ef}.$$

**(c) Screen amplitudes.** Let $(e_1,e_2)$ be an ordered
$\eta$-orthonormal basis of $\Sigma(n,s)$ (which exists by
[[cor-finite-dimensional-inner-product-spaces-have-orthonormal-bases]] applied
to the positive-definite restriction of $\eta$). For a symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor $A$ the **plus and cross amplitudes of $A$ with respect to
$(e_1,e_2)$** are $A_+:=A(e_1,e_1)$ and $A_\times:=A(e_1,e_2)$; if $A$ is
TT with respect to $(n,s)$ in the sense of clause (d) below, then, extending
the screen dual basis to covectors on $\mathbb R^4$ by
$e^i(v):=\eta(e_i,v)$ for $i=1,2$ (so both vanish on $n,s$),

$$A=A_+\bigl(e^1\otimes e^1-e^2\otimes e^2\bigr)+A_\times\bigl(e^1\otimes e^2+e^2\otimes e^1\bigr).$$

For a TT screen tensor $A$, under the rotation
$e_1'=\cos\theta\,e_1+\sin\theta\,e_2$,
$e_2'=-\sin\theta\,e_1+\cos\theta\,e_2$ of the screen basis the amplitudes
transform as $A_+'=A_+\cos2\theta+A_\times\sin2\theta$ and
$A_\times'=-A_+\sin2\theta+A_\times\cos2\theta$. Here $\sin$ and $\cos$
are the power-series functions of [[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]];
expanding $A(e_1',e_1')$ and $A(e_1',e_2')$ by bilinearity and applying the
addition formulas of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]] gives the two
displayed transformations.

**(d) TT tensors and TT perturbations.** A symmetric covariant $2$-tensor
$A$ is **transverse-traceless (TT) with respect to $(n,s)$** when
$A(n,\cdot)=0$, $A(s,\cdot)=0$ and $\eta^{ab}A_{ab}=0$. For a symmetric
field $h$ on a nonempty open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, use the
constant smooth extensions of the fixed component vectors:
$n_q:=n^a\partial_a|_q$ and $s_q:=s^a\partial_a|_q$ for $q\in\Omega$.
Here a symmetric field is a smooth covariant $2$-tensor field with symmetric
components in the sense of [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]. Then
"TT with respect to $(n,s)$" means
$h_q(n_q,\cdot)=h_q(s_q,\cdot)=0$ and $\eta^{ab}h_{ab}(q)=0$ for every
$q\in\Omega$. It is **spatial with respect to $n$** when
$h_q(n_q,\cdot)=0$ for every $q\in\Omega$.

**(e) Scope.** This item fixes the screen, the two projections and the
amplitude terminology, and states the rotation law of clause (c) as part of
the naming. It asserts no property of $\Pi_{n,s}$ (idempotence, rank, image
and trace are proved in the screen-projector lemma of this page), no relation
to the planar perturbations of the plane-wave definition of this page
(established in the gauge-decomposition lemma of this page) and no physical
interpretation of the amplitudes.

Let $(M,g,N)=(\mathbb R^4,\eta,\partial_0)$ be the flat model with its
inertial chart and let $(\varepsilon_1,h,q)$ be a flat linearized family over
an open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ with first-order coefficients
$\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}$ as in [[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]]; write
$R^a{}_{bcd}(\lambda)$ for the curvature components of $g(\lambda)$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]]) and define the
**first-order curvature coefficient**

$$R^{(1)a}{}_{bcd}:=\partial_\lambda R^a{}_{bcd}(\lambda)\big|_{\lambda=0},\qquad R^{(1)}_{abcd}:=\eta_{ae}R^{(1)e}{}_{bcd}.$$

Then:

**(a) General first-order formula.** The coefficient is defined (the
component family is differentiable in $\lambda$ at $0$) and

$$R^{(1)a}{}_{bcd}=\partial_c\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{db}-\partial_d\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{cb},\qquad R^{(1)}_{abcd}=\tfrac12\bigl(\partial_b\partial_ch_{ad}+\partial_a\partial_dh_{bc}-\partial_a\partial_ch_{bd}-\partial_b\partial_dh_{ac}\bigr).$$

**(b) Gauge invariance.** For every smooth covector field $\xi$ on $\Omega$,
with $h'_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a$ the gauge-transformed
perturbation of [[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]] clause (d),
$R^{(1)}_{abcd}(h')=R^{(1)}_{abcd}(h)$: the first-order curvature coefficient
is unchanged by gauge transformations.

**(c) Planar and TT waves.** Let $F=(F_{ab})$ be a smooth planar profile with
$h_{ab}(x)=F_{ab}(u(x))$, $u=x^0-x^3$, and let $n_a=\partial_au$; then

$$R^{(1)}_{abcd}=\tfrac12\bigl(n_bn_cF''_{ad}+n_an_dF''_{bc}-n_an_cF''_{bd}-n_bn_dF''_{ac}\bigr).$$

If the profile is spatial ($F_{0a}=0$ for all $a$), then
$R^{(1)}_{0i0j}=-\tfrac12F''_{ij}$ and, raising indices,
$R^{(1)i}{}_{00j}=+\tfrac12F''{}^i{}_j$. If the profile is TT with amplitudes
$A_+,A_\times$, then $F''$ is supported on the screen with $F''_{11}=A_+''$,
$F''_{22}=-A_+''$, $F''_{12}=F''_{21}=A_\times''$ and all other second
derivatives of the profile zero; in particular

$$R^{(1)}_{0101}=-\tfrac12A_+'',\qquad R^{(1)}_{0102}=-\tfrac12A_\times'',\qquad R^{(1)}_{0202}=+\tfrac12A_+'' .$$

**(d) Contraction to the Ricci coefficient.** For every perturbation $h$,

$$\eta^{ac}R^{(1)}_{abcd}=\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{bd},$$

the right-hand side being the first-order coefficient of
[[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]] clause (b). For a TT planar
perturbation both sides vanish: $\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{bd}=0$ and
$S^{(1)}=0$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $R$ be its
curvature ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]), let
$I,J_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ be intervals with nonempty interior
([[def-interval]]), and let $F:J_0\times I\to M$ be a smooth map. Write
$T:=\partial_tF$ and $J^F:=\partial_rF$; a field along $F$ means a smooth
section of $F^*TM$ over $J_0\times I$, and $D_r,D_t$ are the covariant
derivatives in the two parameters
([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Curvature as the commutator of the two derivatives.** For every smooth
field $V$ along $F$,
$$\bigl(D_tD_r-D_rD_t\bigr)V=R(T,J^F)V .$$

**(b) Geodesic deviation.** Suppose in addition that for every $r\in J_0$ the
curve $t\mapsto F(r,t)$ is a geodesic with affine parameter $t$, that is
$D_tT=0$. Then $D_tJ^F=D_rT$ and
$$D_t^2J^F=R(T,J^F)T .$$
Consequently, for every $r$ the field $t\mapsto J^F(r,t)$ is a Jacobi field
along the geodesic $t\mapsto F(r,t)$
([[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause (b)), and for a geodesic
variation the variation field is a Jacobi field.

**(c) Initial data.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a smooth geodesic and let
$s_0\in I$. For every pair $J_0,J_1\in T_{\gamma(s_0)}M$ there exists exactly
one smooth Jacobi field $J$ along $\gamma$ with
$$J(s_0)=J_0,\qquad D_sJ(s_0)=J_1 .$$
The set of all Jacobi fields along $\gamma$ is a real vector space of
dimension $8$, and $J\mapsto\bigl(J(s_0),D_sJ(s_0)\bigr)$ is a linear
isomorphism onto $T_{\gamma(s_0)}M\oplus T_{\gamma(s_0)}M$.

**(d) The tangential component.** Let $\gamma$ be a smooth geodesic and $J$ a
smooth Jacobi field along it. Then $s\mapsto g(J,\gamma')(s)$ is affine, and
if $\gamma$ is future timelike with $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-1$, the normal
component $J^\perp$ of [[def-gr-jacobi-field-and-conjugate-instant]] clause
(e), explicitly $J^\perp=J+g(J,\gamma')\gamma'$, is again a Jacobi field
along $\gamma$.

Let $a < b$ be reals, let $G : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at every
point of $[a,b]$ as a function on $[a,b]$ (The derivative $f'(c) = \lim_{x \to c} \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c}$ of $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ at a point $c \in A$ that is a limit point of $A$, and differentiability on a set; at $a$ and $b$
this is the one-sided derivative), let $f := G'$, and suppose $f$ is integrable
on $[a,b]$ (The lower and upper Darboux integrals of a bounded $f$ on $[a,b]$ as $\sup_P L(f,P)$ and $\inf_P U(f,P)$, Darboux integrability as their equality, and the notation $\int_a^b f$). Then

$$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

**Both hypotheses are needed and neither is removable.** A function may be
differentiable everywhere with $G'$ not integrable — then the left-hand side does
not exist (an everywhere differentiable function with unbounded derivative) — and an
integrable $f$ need not be the derivative of anything
(the sign function); both witnesses are on the
companion page.

**No continuity of $f$ is assumed**, which is what makes this the working form:
the theorem evaluates $\int_a^b f$ for every integrable derivative, not only for
continuous integrands.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with inertial chart $x$ and
constant metric components $\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and let
$\Omega\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set, identified with its image under
$x$; all components below are taken in the inertial chart. Let $c>0$ be a
real parameter.

**(a) Flat linearized family.** A **flat linearized family over $\Omega$**
consists of a number $\varepsilon_1>0$, a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $h$ on $\Omega$ with components $h_{ab}$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) — the **first-order
perturbation** — and a smooth family $q$ of symmetric component fields
$q_{ab}(\lambda,p)$, defined for $\lambda\in(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)$
and $p\in\Omega$, such that for every $\lambda$ with
$0<|\lambda|<\varepsilon_1$ the component field

$$g_{ab}(\lambda,p):=\eta_{ab}+\lambda\,h_{ab}(p)+\lambda^2\,q_{ab}(\lambda,p)$$

is the component field of a smooth Lorentzian metric $g(\lambda)$ on
$\Omega$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; $q$ is the **normalized remainder**. The
family is thus normalized so that $g(0)=\eta$ is its value at
$\lambda=0$ and $h=\partial_\lambda g(\lambda)|_{\lambda=0}$. No assumption
is made that $g(\lambda)$ solves any field equation; the metrics $g(\lambda)$
are the mathematical input of the linearization.

**(b) First-order coefficients.** Let $A(\lambda)$ stand for any of the
component families $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(g(\lambda))$,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g(\lambda))$, $S(g(\lambda))$,
$G_{ab}(g(\lambda))$ of the metric-selected connection of $g(\lambda)$; these
are smooth in $(\lambda,p)$ because the Christoffel symbols, the curvature
components and the inverse metric are smooth functions of the metric
components and their derivatives
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Define the **first-order
coefficients**

$$\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}:=\partial_\lambda\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},\quad \operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}:=\partial_\lambda\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},$$
$$S^{(1)}:=\partial_\lambda S(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}:=\partial_\lambda G_{ab}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0}.$$

**(c) Index conventions.** Indices on first-order quantities are raised and
lowered with the flat metric $\eta$ and its inverse $\eta^{ab}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]): $\partial^a:=\eta^{ab}\partial_b$,
$h^{ab}:=\eta^{ac}\eta^{bd}h_{cd}$, and

$$\Box:=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b=-\partial_0^2+\partial_1^2+\partial_2^2+\partial_3^2$$

is the **d'Alembertian** of the flat metric, applied componentwise to
component families. The **trace** of $h$ and the **trace-reversed
perturbation** are

$$h:=\eta^{ab}h_{ab},\qquad \bar h_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\tfrac12\,h\,\eta_{ab} .$$

The inverse passage is the same formula, $\bar h_{ab}$'s trace being
$\eta^{ab}\bar h_{ab}=h-2h=-h$: explicitly

$$h_{ab}=\bar h_{ab}-\tfrac12\,\eta_{ab}\,\eta^{cd}\bar h_{cd} .$$

**(d) Gauge transformation.** For a smooth covector field $\xi_b$ on
$\Omega$ define the **gauge-transformed first-order perturbation**

$$h'_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a .$$

This is the first-order perturbation of the pullback family
$\Phi_{-\lambda}^*g(\lambda)$ along the local flows $\Phi_s$ of the vector
field $\xi^a=\eta^{ab}\xi_b$, that is, the perturbation produced by the
infinitesimal chart change $x'^a=x^a+\lambda\xi^a$ and re-read on the fixed
inertial chart; the transformation of the metric components displayed here
is the linearization of the Jacobian transformation law, and
its consequences for $\bar h$ and for $\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}$, $S^{(1)}$
and $G^{(1)}$ are proved separately on this page (the first-order curvature
and gauge theorem that follows this definition).
The perturbation $h$ is **in harmonic gauge** (also called de Donder gauge)
when

$$\partial^a\bar h_{ab}=0 .$$

**(e) Scope.** This item fixes the objects of the flat linearization: the
normalized family, the first-order coefficients defined as exact
$\lambda$-derivatives, the trace reversal, the d'Alembertian and the gauge
transformation. It asserts no explicit formula for the first-order
coefficients, no existence of a gauge representative satisfying (d), no
solution of any linearized field equation and no physical interpretation;
those are separate results. The notation is tied to the inertial chart: a
change of chart is a different operation from the gauge transformation (d),
which changes the metric family inside the fixed chart.

Let $F(t,x,\lambda)$ be jointly $C^\infty$ in $(t,x,\lambda)$ on an open time-state-parameter
domain. Near any base data $(t_0,x_0,\lambda_0)$ there are a compact time
interval $I$ and a neighbourhood $W$ of $(x_0,\lambda_0)$ such that, for every
$(y,\lambda)\in W$, the solution of

$$x'(t)=F(t,x(t),\lambda),\qquad x(t_0)=y,$$

is defined on $I$, and the resulting solution map is smooth in the pair
$(y,\lambda)$.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Apply [F5] to each smooth tensor component $C_{AB}(u,x)$ at the fixed angular point. Since $N_{AB}=\partial_uC_{AB}$, $C_{AB}(u_2,x)-C_{AB}(u_1,x)=\int_{u_1}^{u_2}N_{AB}(u,x)\,du$. This is the first identity.

In the adapted frame of [A2], the plane-wave curvature supplier gives $R^{(1)A}{}_{00B}=\tfrac12\partial_u^2H^A{}_B$ ([F3]); the Jacobi equation of [F4] with initial screen value $s_0^Ae_A$ and zero initial derivative therefore has this forcing at first order, since the flat background curvature is zero and the basis is constant. Thus its formal first-order response obeys exactly the defining equation for $\delta s^A$ in the Statement. No finite-amplitude error estimate is used.

For the quantitative clause set $T:=u_2-u_1>0$. Choose a compact state neighborhood of $(\gamma_0(u),\partial_0)$, $u\in[u_1,u_2]$, whose position projection lies inside the specified open tube, with positive margins about this compact graph. By [F6] and [F8], the Christoffels are smooth jointly and vanish at $\lambda=0$, so their norms on this neighborhood are at most $C|\lambda|$ for small $|\lambda|$. The coordinate geodesic system is $x'=v$, $v'^a=-\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(\lambda,x)v^bv^c$. By [F7] it has a local smooth solution from the stated unit initial velocity. As long as it stays in this neighborhood, the bounded velocity range gives $|v-\partial_0|\le|v(u_1)-\partial_0|+C_1|\lambda|T$ and $|x-\gamma_0|\le T\sup|v-\partial_0|$. Choose $|\lambda|$ small enough to keep both bounds strictly inside the chosen margins. The solution cannot leave the neighborhood. A putative finite maximal endpoint would have a state limit there, since its derivative is bounded; [F7] at that interior limit extends the solution, a contradiction. Thus it exists on the full interval. A finite subdivision and [F7] give smooth dependence on $\lambda$ throughout it. The unit timelike norm is preserved by [F8], and $\partial_0$ remains timelike on a smaller fixed tube for small $|\lambda|$, fixing the future cone.

Integrate the linearized equation twice, using $\delta s(u_1)=\partial_u\delta s(u_1)=0$, to obtain
$$\delta s^A(u_2)=\frac12\int_{u_1}^{u_2}(u_2-v)\,\partial_v^2H^A{}_B(v)\,s_0^B\,dv.$$
Integration by parts gives $\delta s^A(u_2)=\tfrac12[\Delta H^A{}_B-(u_2-u_1)\partial_uH^A{}_B(u_1)]s_0^B$. Since $H=C/r+\rho$, the endpoint condition $N_{AB}(u_1)=0$ and the $K_1r^{-2}$ bound give $\partial_uH(u_1)=O(r^{-2})$; the $K_0r^{-2}$ bound gives $\Delta H=\Delta C/r+O(r^{-2})$. This proves the stated displacement estimate, with constants depending on $u_2-u_1$ and $K_0,K_1$.

Integrating the linearized equation once gives $\partial_u\delta s^A(u_2)=\tfrac12(\partial_uH^A{}_B(u_2)-\partial_uH^A{}_B(u_1))s_0^B$. At both endpoints the leading derivative is $N^A{}_B/r=0$, and the $K_1r^{-2}$ bound controls the remainder derivatives. This proves the endpoint velocity estimate.

Smooth Gram-Schmidt at the initial point gives the chosen spatial orthonormal frame, since its projected Gram matrix is positive at $\lambda=0$ and remains positive nearby. Parallel transport solves $E'{}^a=-\Gamma^a{}_{bc}v^bE^c$, a linear equation with bounded smooth coefficients along the compact geodesic. Local solutions from [F7] extend over the interval: the equation gives $(|E|^2)'\le2C|E|^2$, so differentiating $e^{-2C(u-u_1)}|E|^2$ bounds $|E|$ by $|E(u_1)|e^{CT}$ and prevents escape at a finite endpoint, and local uniqueness patches a finite subdivision. They depend smoothly on $\lambda$ and remain orthonormal and orthogonal to the geodesic tangent by [F8]. The Jacobi initial-data result [F4] gives a unique field $J_\lambda$ with the stated covariant rest data. It is an actual variation field: choose an initial chart curve with tangent $J_\lambda(u_1)$, parallel-transport the initial timelike velocity along it, and issue geodesics from those data. The same compact-state argument as step 1.3 supplies the resulting smooth geodesic variation on the whole interval for sufficiently small variation parameter. Torsion-freeness gives initial covariant derivative zero, so uniqueness in [F4] identifies its variation field with $J_\lambda$.

Write $x_\lambda\in\mathbb R^3$ for the spatial components of $J_\lambda$ in that parallel frame; its time component is zero because $g(J_\lambda,\gamma_\lambda')$ is affine with zero initial value and derivative by [F4]. Its exact equation is
$$x_\lambda''=K_\lambda x_\lambda,\qquad (K_\lambda)^i{}_j=g_\lambda(E_{i,\lambda},R_\lambda(\gamma_\lambda',E_{j,\lambda})\gamma_\lambda'),\qquad x_\lambda(u_1)=x_0:=(s_0^1,s_0^2,0),\quad x_\lambda'(u_1)=0.$$

$$K_\lambda=\lambda \mathcal K_1+\lambda^2L_\lambda,\qquad (\mathcal K_1)^A{}_B=\tfrac12H''{}^A{}_B,$$

Assume Countable Choice for the smooth Lorentzian tangent-bundle conventions of the suppliers. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, $r_0>0$, and $\mathcal E=I\times(r_0,\infty)\times S^2$, where $S^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ has its unit round metric $q_{AB}$ and area form $d\Omega$. Let $D_A$ be the Levi-Civita covariant derivative of $q$, and raise angular indices with $q^{AB}$. A **Bondi-Sachs end** is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $\mathcal E$ written in coordinates $(u,r,x^A)$, $A,B=1,2$, as

$$g=-\left(e^{2\beta}\frac Vr-r^2\gamma_{AB}U^AU^B\right)du^2-2e^{2\beta}du\,dr-2r^2\gamma_{AB}U^Bdu\,dx^A+r^2\gamma_{AB}dx^A dx^B,$$

where $\beta,V,U^A,\gamma_{AB}$ are smooth, $\gamma_{AB}$ is positive definite, $\gamma^{AC}\gamma_{CB}=\delta^A_B$, and $\det(\gamma_{AB})=\det(q_{AB})$. Thus $u=\mathrm{constant}$ are outgoing null hypersurfaces, $r$ is the area radius, and $x^A$ are constant along their null generators. This Bondi gauge has $g_{rr}=g_{rA}=0$.

A **smooth Bondi expansion** is such an end with the differentiated uniform expansions

$$\gamma_{AB}=q_{AB}+\frac{C_{AB}(u,x)}r+\frac{P_{AB}(u,x)}{r^2}+O(r^{-3}),\qquad \beta=O(r^{-2}),\qquad U^A=\frac{U^A_{(2)}(u,x)}{r^2}+\frac{U^A_{(3)}(u,x)}{r^3}+O(r^{-4}),\qquad V=r-2m(u,x)+\frac{V_{(1)}(u,x)}r+O(r^{-2}).$$

Here $C_{AB}$, $P_{AB}$ and the displayed coefficients are smooth sphere fields on $I$; the determinant gauge imposes $q^{AB}C_{AB}=0$ and $q^{AB}P_{AB}=\tfrac12 C_{AB}C^{AB}$. For every compact $I'\subset I$, angular chart compact set, and derivative multi-index $\alpha$ of total order at most two, the partial derivatives of each $O(r^{-k})$ remainder obey $\partial_u^{\alpha_u}D^{\alpha_x}\partial_r^{\alpha_r}O(r^{-k})=O(r^{-k-\alpha_r})$ uniformly as $r\to\infty$. Define the **mass aspect** by $m(u,x):=-\tfrac12\lim_{r\to\infty}(V(u,r,x)-r)$, the **Bondi shear** by $C_{AB}=\lim_{r\to\infty}r(\gamma_{AB}-q_{AB})$, the **Bondi news** by $N_{AB}:=\partial_u C_{AB}$, and the **geometric Bondi mass** by $m_B(u):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}m(u,x)\,d\Omega$. The future null boundary used here is the formal $r\to\infty$ boundary $\mathcal I^+=I\times S^2$ with coordinates $(u,x^A)$; no conformal completion is included in this definition.

A **vacuum Bondi expansion** is a smooth Bondi expansion whose Ricci tensor vanishes identically on the supplied end: $\operatorname{Ric}_g(p)=0$ for every $p\in\mathcal E$. Equivalently, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(u,r,x)=0$ for every pair $a,b\in\{u,r,1,2\}$ at every point of every Bondi coordinate chart, with no cosmological term. The curvature convention is $R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$, $R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=R^a{}_{bcd}\partial_a$, and $\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}=R^a{}_{bad}$. This is a condition on the supplied metric, not an assertion of existence for prescribed boundary coefficients. Imposing only finitely many asymptotic coefficient equations does not assert membership in this vacuum subclass; formal boundary-data examples must state separately which equations they impose.

Assume Countable Choice for the smooth Lorentzian boundary conventions inherited from [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]]. On its formal boundary $\mathcal I^+=I\times S^2$, let $\ell_{\mathcal I}=\partial_u$ be the null-generator direction and let $q_{AB}$ be the unit round metric on the cuts; the degenerate boundary metric is $q_{AB}dx^A dx^B$ with kernel $\mathbb R\ell_{\mathcal I}$. A **fixed Bondi frame** here means the chosen Bondi-Sachs chart and gauge $(u,r,x^A)$ of [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]], including $g_{rr}=g_{rA}=0$ and $\det\gamma=\det q$, with the round cut metric $q_{AB}$ held fixed. It is a chart/gauge choice, not an observer congruence or tetrad. An **infinitesimal supertranslation** is the asymptotic vector field parametrized by a smooth real function $f:S^2\to\mathbb R$ whose leading boundary action is $\delta_fu=f(x)$ and whose leading bulk generator is

$$\xi_f=f\,\partial_u-\frac1rD^Af\,\partial_A+\frac12D^AD_Af\,\partial_r+O(r^{-1})\partial_u+O(r^{-2})\partial_A+O(r^{-1})\partial_r.$$

The displayed leading terms preserve Bondi gauge and the fixed round cut metric to the asymptotic orders used here; the omitted terms are not part of this definition. We use the active convention $\delta_f=\mathcal L_{\xi_f}$. Its action on the shear and news of [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]] is

$$\delta_f C_{AB}=fN_{AB}-2D_AD_Bf+q_{AB}D^CD_Cf,\qquad \delta_f N_{AB}=f\,\partial_uN_{AB}.$$

The **finite active boundary supertranslation** with parameter $f$ is the map $\Phi_f(u,x)=(u+f(x),x)$ on
$$\mathcal D_f:=\{(u,x)\in I\times S^2:u+f(x)\in I\}.$$
It is a diffeomorphism from $\mathcal D_f$ onto $\mathcal D_{-f}$, with inverse $\Phi_{-f}$. If $I=\mathbb R$, it is a diffeomorphism of all of $\mathcal I^+$; for a shorter retarded-time interval the action is defined on this overlap only. In the same active convention, its induced action on the boundary shear and news is

$$C^{(f)}_{AB}(u,x)=C_{AB}(u+f(x),x)-2D_AD_Bf(x)+q_{AB}D^CD_Cf(x),\qquad N^{(f)}_{AB}(u,x)=N_{AB}(u+f(x),x),\quad (u,x)\in\mathcal D_f.$$

Differentiating these formulas for the parameter $tf$ at $t=0$ recovers the infinitesimal formulas above. This definition gives only the boundary action and induced shear/news; it does not specify the full finite bulk coordinate transformation.

The function $f$ carries length units when the retarded coordinate $u$ is read in SI geometric coordinates; the sphere derivatives and angular coordinates are dimensionless. The Hessian term is trace-free because $q^{AB}q_{AB}=2$. When $N_{AB}=0$, an infinitesimal supertranslation therefore changes a time-independent shear by the sphere trace-free Hessian while leaving the news zero.

Assume Countable Choice for the smooth Lorentzian bundle conventions of the suppliers. Let a vacuum Bondi expansion be as in [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]], with $R_{ab}=0$ in the curvature convention of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Then, for the mass aspect $m$, shear $C_{AB}$, news $N_{AB}=\partial_uC_{AB}$, unit sphere metric $q_{AB}$ and its Levi-Civita derivative $D_A$ specified there,

$$\partial_um=\frac14D_AD_BN^{AB}-\frac18N_{AB}N^{AB}.$$

The identity is the leading supplementary vacuum Einstein coefficient at future null infinity; it is not an exact finite-radius equation.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: The restriction $Y=\tfrac12(3x_3^2-1)$ is smooth on the sphere because it is the restriction of a polynomial. Put $T_{AB}:=D_AD_BY-\tfrac12q_{AB}D^2Y$. Its trace is zero. At $\theta=\pi/2$, $D_\theta D_\theta Y=3$, $D_\phi D_\phi Y=0$ and $D^2Y=3$, so $T_{\theta\theta}=3/2$; hence $T$ is nonzero.

With $t=u+r$, the metric $g_0=-du^2-2du\,dr+r^2q$ becomes $-dt^2+dr^2+r^2q$, the Minkowski metric in spherical spatial coordinates. Thus its Bondi data are exactly $C_{AB}=N_{AB}=m=0$. Since $f=aY$ is independent of $u$, [F2] gives $C^{(f)}_{AB}= -2aD_AD_BY+a q_{AB}D^2Y=-2aT_{AB}$ and $N^{(f)}_{AB}=0$. We use only these as formal boundary data; we do not assert that they are the coefficients of a finite transformed vacuum metric.

Set $m(u,x)=0$ for the formal data. With $N_{AB}=0$, [F3] is satisfied and $m_B(u)=\tfrac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}m\,d\Omega=0$, so $dm_B/du=0$. The shear $C^{(f)}_{AB}=-2aT_{AB}$ is independent of $u$, hence $\Delta C_{AB}=0$ on every interval. These conclusions follow directly from the stipulated data and constraint; neither vacuum mass-loss nor the memory proposition is invoked.
